text:
maria: ran a round of compaction experiments on hetero-gpu nodes this morning. saw unexpected p99 spikes on sparse embedding workloads.
kevin: unexpected how big? numbers?
maria: p95 stable, but p99 jumped ~2.8x for ~90-150s windows when compactor was active. average latency and throughput unchanged.
oliver: any CPU/IO patterns in the traces?
maria: traces attached (summarized):

```
compactor: burst loop ~3800ms, move_batch avg 48 entries
prefetch threads: 6 -> saw 80-120ms stalls aligned to compactor bursts
node cpu steal: +10-15% concurrent with compaction
mutex contention spikes on slab-manager lock
```

maria: also noticed many small page-move ops (<1KB) which produce lots of metadata churn.
anika: sounds like small-object relocation thrash. allocator fragmentation shape?
maria: workload alloc histogram: 70% allocations <=256B, 25% 256B-4KB, rare >64KB. hot working set is small but scattered across slabs and tenants.
kevin: small moves are expensive because of cross-NUMA page pins and cacheline churn. two directions: reduce move frequency (less aggressive compaction) or make moves cheaper (batch metadata updates, async refcounts).
oliver: or avoid moving tiny objects entirely: implement a slab-local coalesce operation that compacts free slots within a slab without touching other pages. cheaper and avoids pin/unpin.
anika: that requires allocator exposing a new op: try_coalesce_local(slab_id) -> returns reclaimed_bytes. small refactor but low-risk.
maria: did quick cpulimit test: restricting compactor to 25% CPU reduced p99 spike amplitude to ~1.15x baseline but compaction throughput dropped ~6x. so we trade immediate SLO vs long-term frag.
kevin: tradeoff is clear. if we throttle, frag accumulates; if we run full-speed, transient SLO breaks. can we be adaptive?
oliver: propose adaptive backoff: compactor watches serve_p99 and admission margin (available qps slack). if p99 > target*1.15 or margin < 12% -> increase sleep between cycles exponentially; if margin > 30% and frag level high -> temporarily ramp up.
anika: need metrics: compaction.moves_per_sec, compaction.avg_move_size, frag_percent (w/ heatmap), compaction.cpu_pct, and serve_p99 per-tenant. also a boolean escalated_maintenance flag.
maria: implemented a quick feedback loop locally: backoff based on p99 threshold and CPU steal. result: p99 stayed within 1.1x baseline, compaction kept pace enough to prevent immediate frag explosion, but long-term fragmentation reduction slowed.
kevin: could we hybridize: fast maintenance compacts during predictable low-traffic windows (00:00–04:00) and cooperative incremental compaction during normal hours? schedule should be tenant-aware to avoid interfering with small-traffic tenants.
anika: tenant-aware scheduling needs compaction metadata per-tenant (last_compact_ts, frag_ratio). ties into leases/reservations to get safe quiet windows. bigger infra change but valuable.
oliver: I'll spike on allocator-local-coalesce POC — implement try_coalesce_local and a cheap heuristics to prefer slabs with >50% free slots fragmentation. aim to avoid cross-page moves for objects <=1KB. will pair with anika for tests.
maria: I'll open the adaptive backoff PR (branch feature/compaction-feedback) with telemetry and a canary rollout plan. target: canary on 2 non-prod racks for 48h, monitor p99 and moves/sec.
kevin: ensure we have kill-switch flags: compaction.disable_backoff and compaction.force_maintenance (manual). also name the backoff ratio flag compaction.slo_backoff_ratio (0.15 default).
anika: add runbook entries: when to force maintenance, how to read compaction heatmap, and escalation path if p99 persists.
maria: CI triggered for branch feature/compaction-feedback (#3780). tests: unit x138, integration x14.
ci-bot: build queued for feature/compaction-feedback (#3780).
kevin: good. timeline?
maria: PR by EOD, canary next day. oliver, you'll own the coalesce POC; aim for spike + perf numbers in next sprint.
oliver: got it. will prototype in slab manager and run microbenchmarks: move_count, CPU delta, p99 overlay.
anika: if coalesce POC looks promising, we can adopt micro-compact as default for small-object heavy tenants.
kevin: final note: make sure compaction telemetry is tagged by tenant and node so we can correlate regressions quickly.
maria: agreed. I'll add labels. thanks team. :thumbsup:
